mainTopic: Holes and spouts in wine barrels on שבת, felt cloths, and a new משנה on cooling, warming, and drying wet clothes
overview: This amud covers several short שבת topics, mostly about wine barrels, and then begins a new משנה. First, the הלכה follows the יש אומרים: you may not even widen an existing hole in a barrel. Reopening an old sealed hole is allowed only if the hole was for straining the wine. רב חסדא and רבא disagree about which holes count as straining, and אביי supports רבא with a ברייתא about sealed doorways. Next, רב and שמואל argue about putting a reed spout into a barrel. The argument is only about a reed that was cut before שבת but never fitted, and the הלכה follows רבי יאשיה, who permits it. Then come short discussions of sealing a hole with oil, using a myrtle leaf as a spout, and wearing felt cloths, where the גמרא shows that רב actually permitted the felt. A new משנה then allows cooling food and water, warming water in the sun, and drying wet clothes in private. The amud ends with רב's rule that something forbidden because of מראית העין is forbidden even in private, and the start of a statement by רב הונא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the יש אומרים forbid widening a hole
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the reason for the first view (משום ריחשא). It then explains why the יש אומרים forbid even widening an existing hole: someone might widen a poorly made hole in a chicken coop, which would complete it.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...because of the vermin. And the 'some say' who rule that one may not add to a hole: sometimes a person did not make the opening properly at first, and he comes to widen it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the reason it began on the previous page. It then explains why the יש אומרים forbid even making an old hole bigger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule for barrels is a גזירה, a protective decree based on holes in a chicken coop. There, widening a hole that was never made properly would actually finish it, and that is real מלאכה. The יש אומרים worry that allowing a barrel hole to be widened could lead someone to widen a coop hole.

keyTerms.meaning: Vermin or creeping things. Some explain it as stifling heat that harms the chickens.
'Some say.' An unnamed opinion in a ברייתא.
One may not add to, or widen, an existing hole.

phrases.english: because of the vermin.
phrases.notes: This ends the explanation from the previous page about holes in a chicken coop.

phrases.english: And the 'some say' who rule one may not add to a hole —
sometimes he did not make it properly at first,
and he comes to widen it.
phrases.notes: Widening it then finishes the opening, which is a forbidden act of completion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation of the ברייתא from the previous page.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the reason behind the protective decree
steps.terutzMaskana: Widening is forbidden because someone might come to finish an improperly made coop hole.

steps.title: The הלכה follows the יש אומרים
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבי יוחנן, rules like the יש אומרים: one may not widen an existing hole on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן taught in the name of רבי יוחנן: the הלכה follows the 'some say.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives the final ruling: we follow the stricter view of the יש אומרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of this ruling, the practical הלכה is that even adding to an existing hole is forbidden. This is stricter than the first opinion in the ברייתא, which allowed it.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה: you may not make a new hole in a barrel on שבת, and you may not widen an existing one either.

phrases.aramaic: דָּרֵשׁ רַב נַחְמָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
phrases.english: Rav Nachman taught in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
The halacha follows the 'some say.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two views that were just explained.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One may not widen an existing hole in a barrel on שבת.

steps.title: Reopening an old hole is allowed only if it was made for straining
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's rule that everyone allows reopening an old hole. שמואל limits it: this applies only to a hole made to strain the wine, not to one connected to reinforcing the barrel.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And all agree that one may open an old hole from the start.' רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: This was taught only about a spot made for straining. But a spot related to reinforcing is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the ברייתא. שמואל then narrows it, so it does not apply to every old hole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reopening an old hole is normally not 'making' anything new. שמואל says this only holds when the hole was meant to strain the wine. If the hole's status is tied to strengthening the barrel, opening it is like fixing a כלי, so it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: An old hole that was sealed up.
'They only taught this about...' A formula that limits a rule.
To strain the wine away from its sediment.
To reinforce or strengthen the barrel.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read לשמר as 'to guard.' Here it means straining wine away from its dregs (שמרים).

phrases.english: And all agree that one may open an old hole from the start.
phrases.notes: A quotation from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בִּמְקוֹם הֶעָשׂוּי לְשַׁמֵּר,
phrases.english: They taught this only about a spot made for straining,
but one related to reinforcing is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בִּמְקוֹם הֶעָשׂוּי לְשַׁמֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new clause of the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reopening an old hole is allowed only when the hole was meant for straining.

steps.title: What counts as straining and what counts as reinforcing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a definition of the two categories שמואל just used.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a case of 'straining,' and what is a case of 'reinforcing'?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup question. The גמרא asks for a clear definition, and the next two steps give two different answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's rule only works if we know how to tell the two kinds of holes apart. The question opens a disagreement between רב חסדא and רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How do we picture it?

phrases.english: What is a case of 'straining,'
and what is a case of 'reinforcing'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for definitions of the terms in שמואל's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to tell a hole for straining from a hole for reinforcing.

steps.title: רב חסדא: it depends on the wine level
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says a hole above the wine is for straining, and a hole below the wine is for reinforcing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Above the wine, that is straining. Below the wine, that is reinforcing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives his definition: the dividing line is the level of the wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine pours out through a low hole, so a sealed hole below the wine level is part of what keeps the barrel strong and whole. Reopening it would be like repairing the כלי, so it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Above the level of the wine.
Below the level of the wine.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Above the wine — that is for straining,
below the wine — that is for reinforcing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא לְמַעְלָה מִן הַיַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The wine level divides straining (above) from reinforcing (below).

steps.title: רבא: only a hole below the sediment is for reinforcing
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees. Even a hole below the wine counts as straining. Only a hole below the sediment counts as reinforcing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Below the wine is also straining. And what is reinforcing? For example, where it was pierced below the sediment.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different, more lenient definition that moves the line down to the sediment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine can still be drawn through a hole that sits below the wine but above the dregs, so that hole is still a working opening. Only a hole below the sediment could never be used to draw clear wine. Sealing it is therefore really about strengthening the barrel.

keyTerms.meaning: Sediment, the dregs of the wine.
For example; as in a case where.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: לְמַטָּה מִן הַיַּיִן נָמֵי זֶהוּ לְשַׁמֵּר.
phrases.english: Below the wine is also for straining.
And what is a case of reinforcing?
For example, where it was pierced below the sediment.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר לְמַטָּה מִן הַיַּיִן נָמֵי זֶהוּ לְשַׁמֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב חסדא's definition.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only a hole below the sediment counts as reinforcing. Anything above the sediment is for straining.

steps.title: אביי brings a ברייתא about sealed doorways to support רבא
steps.stepSummary: אביי shows רבא a ברייתא. A sealed doorway still counts as a doorway, both for the four cubits when dividing a courtyard and for spreading טומאה. Only breaking the doorposts cancels it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רבא: A ברייתא was taught that supports you. A house with a sealed entrance still has four cubits. If he broke its doorposts, it does not have four cubits. A house with sealed entrances does not make everything around it impure. If he broke its doorposts, it makes everything around it impure.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי supports רבא with a ברייתא. It shows that an opening keeps its status until it is clearly and fully cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sealed doorway still counts as a doorway because it can easily be reopened. It loses that status only when the doorposts are destroyed. In the same way, a sealed hole that can still be used to draw wine (anywhere above the sediment) keeps its status as a 'straining' hole, just as רבא said.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that supports you.
A house with a sealed doorway.
The four cubits in front of a doorway that its owner receives when a courtyard is divided.
Spreads טומאת מת all around it, not only through its doorways.

steps.confusionAlert: Look closely at the טומאה case. A house that still has a doorway spreads טומאה only through that doorway, so it does not make everything around it impure. Once the doorposts are broken there is no doorway at all, so the טומאה spreads on every side.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches a general idea: something closed up but easy to reopen keeps its status until it is clearly cancelled.

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rava:
A baraita was taught that supports you:

phrases.aramaic: בַּיִת סָתוּם — יֵשׁ לוֹ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת,
phrases.english: A sealed house still has four cubits,

phrases.aramaic: פָּרַץ אֶת פַּצִּימָיו — אֵין לוֹ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת.
phrases.english: if he broke its doorposts, it does not have four cubits.

phrases.aramaic: בַּיִת סָתוּם — אֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא כׇּל סְבִיבָיו,
phrases.english: A sealed house does not make all its surroundings impure,

phrases.aramaic: פָּרַץ אֶת פַּצִּימָיו — מְטַמֵּא כׇּל סְבִיבָיו.
phrases.english: if he broke its doorposts, it makes all its surroundings impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's definition.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that a hole keeps its 'straining' status unless it is clearly useless for drawing wine.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: a sealed doorway keeps its status until its doorposts are broken.

steps.title: רב and שמואל argue about inserting a reed
steps.stepSummary: רב forbids putting a reed (used as a spout) into a barrel on שבת. שמואל permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A reed: רב forbade and שמואל permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins: a dispute about putting a reed tube into a barrel so wine can flow out of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dispute is stated in short form here. The next steps explain exactly what case they are arguing about.

keyTerms.meaning: A reed used as a tube or spout for drawing wine.

phrases.english: A reed: Rav forbade, and Shmuel permits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, related topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב forbids inserting a reed into a barrel on שבת, and שמואל permits it.

steps.title: Where רב and שמואל agree
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees that cutting a reed fresh is forbidden, and that putting an already fitted reed back is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Cutting it from the start: everyone agrees it is forbidden. Putting it back: everyone agrees it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the dispute by setting aside the two cases where everyone agrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting a reed to make a spout creates a new כלי, so it is clearly forbidden. Putting back a reed that already fitted is just returning it to use, so it is clearly permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees; no one disputes it.
Putting back, returning to its place.

phrases.aramaic: מְחַתֵּךְ לְכַתְּחִלָּה — דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דַּאֲסִיר.
phrases.english: Cutting it from the start — everyone agrees it is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: אַהְדּוֹרֵי — דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דִּשְׁרֵי.
phrases.english: Putting it back — everyone agrees it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the dispute that was just stated.

steps.title: The real dispute: a reed cut but never fitted
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל argue only about a reed that was already cut but never fitted. רב makes a גזירה in case someone comes to cut one. שמואל does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they argue is a reed that was cut but not yet fitted. The one who forbids makes a decree, lest one come to cut it from the start. The one who permits does not make a decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states exactly where the dispute lies and gives each side's reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting a cut reed into the barrel is not a מלאכה in itself. רב forbids it anyway, out of concern that people will start cutting reeds on שבת. שמואל sees no need for that extra protective decree.

keyTerms.meaning: And not yet fitted or prepared for use.

steps.whatToRemember: Cutting a reed is forbidden and returning a fitted reed is permitted. The argument is only about a cut but unfitted reed: רב forbids it as a גזירה, and שמואל permits it.

phrases.english: Where they argue is when it was cut but not fitted:
The one who forbids holds that we make a decree,
lest he come to cut it from the start,
and the one who permits holds that we do not make a decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the case in dispute after the agreed cases were set aside.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The dispute is whether to make a גזירה against fitting a reed that was already cut.

steps.title: An older dispute that matches רב and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a dispute between תנאים that matches the argument between רב and שמואל about the reed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute between תנאים: You may not cut a reed tube on יום טוב, and certainly not on שבת. If an already cut tube fell out, you may put it back on שבת, and certainly on יום טוב. And רבי יאשיה is lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the argument between רב and שמואל is not new. It brings a ברייתא where תנאים seem to argue about the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא has three parts: cutting a new reed is forbidden, putting back a fallen reed is allowed, and רבי יאשיה is 'lenient'. It does not yet say what רבי יאשיה is lenient about. The next steps work that out.

keyTerms.meaning: It is like a dispute of תנאים
A reed tube, used as a spout

steps.confusionAlert: The word (אֵין) is in parentheses because it is crossed out in the corrected text. Read the line as 'you MAY put it back', not 'you may not'.

phrases.english: It is like a dispute of Tannaim:
One may not cut a reed tube on a Festival,
and needless to say, on Shabbat.
If it fell out, one may put it back on Shabbat,
phrases.notes: The word אין in parentheses should be left out, so read it without it.

phrases.english: and needless to say, on a Festival.
And Rabbi Yoshiya is lenient.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the רב and שמואל argument from step 10 has a parallel among תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: The argument between רב and שמואל about a cut but never-fitted reed
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with a lenient opinion of רבי יאשיה

steps.title: What is רבי יאשיה lenient about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which part of the ברייתא רבי יאשיה is commenting on.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יאשיה: which part is he talking about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question: which case is רבי יאשיה being lenient about? This sets up the next step, which tests each possibility.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only says 'רבי יאשיה is lenient' without saying where. Until we know this, we cannot match it to רב and שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: On which one? Which part is it referring to?
The תנא who gives the lenient opinion

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoshiya — on which part is he commenting?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to clarify the unclear lenient opinion in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case in the ברייתא רבי יאשיה is lenient about

steps.title: He cannot be talking about the first or last case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects both obvious readings: רבי יאשיה cannot permit cutting a reed, and he cannot be adding anything to putting it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he refers to the first part, isn't the person making a vessel? Rather, the last part? The first תנא also allows that!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first case and the last case of the ברייתא, and shows that neither works for רבי יאשיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting a reed is making a new vessel (מתקן מנא), which nobody would permit. Putting back a fallen reed is already allowed by the תנא קמא, so being 'lenient' there adds nothing. So רבי יאשיה must be talking about some third case.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a text
The last part of a text
Making or fixing a vessel, forbidden on שבת
The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: If you say on the first clause — isn't he making a vessel?

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אַסֵּיפָא — תַּנָּא קַמָּא נָמֵי מִישְׁרֵא קָשָׁרֵי?
phrases.english: Rather, on the last clause — the first Tanna also permits it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the two obvious answers to the question in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Both the first-clause and last-clause readings of רבי יאשיה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The first reading would permit making a vessel; the second would make רבי יאשיה say nothing new.

steps.title: They argue about a cut reed that was never fitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the תנאים argue about a reed already cut but never fitted: the תנא קמא makes a גזירה, רבי יאשיה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the difference between them is a reed that was cut but not yet fitted. One master holds we make a גזירה, and the other holds we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its answer: רבי יאשיה is lenient about the in-between case, a reed that was cut before שבת but never fitted into a barrel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is exactly the case רב and שמואל argue about in step 10. The תנא קמא forbids it like רב, worried someone will come to cut a new one. רבי יאשיה permits it like שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא דַּחֲתִיכָה וְלָא מְתַקְּנָא אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ,
phrases.english: Rather, a reed that was cut but not fitted is the difference between them:
One master holds: we make a decree.
And one master holds: we do not make a decree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דַּחֲתִיכָה וְלָא מְתַקְּנָא אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the two readings in step 13, gives the correct reading.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יאשיה permits a cut but never-fitted reed, and the תנא קמא forbids it as a גזירה.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יאשיה
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא son of רב אידי taught in the name of רבי יוחנן that the הלכה follows רבי יאשיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא son of רב אידי taught publicly in the name of רבי יוחנן: the הלכה follows רבי יאשיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling: we follow the lenient view of רבי יאשיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So a reed cut before שבת but never fitted may be put into a barrel on שבת. This matches the view of שמואל and not the גזירה of רב.
steps.whatToRemember: Cutting a new reed is forbidden. Putting back a fitted reed is allowed. A cut but never-fitted reed is argued about, and the הלכה follows רבי יאשיה (and שמואל) to permit it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the practical answer to the whole reed discussion from steps 8 to 15.

phrases.aramaic: דָּרַשׁ רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידֵּי
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha, son of Rav Idi, taught publicly
in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yoshiya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the dispute explained in step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A cut but never-fitted reed may be used as a spout on שבת.

steps.title: רב and שמואל argue about sealing a hole with oil
steps.stepSummary: Returning to the משנה about a barrel with a hole, רב forbids sealing it with oil and שמואל permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And if it had a hole, etc.' About oil: רב forbids and שמואל permits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the next line of the משנה, which says you may not seal a hole in a barrel with wax. It brings a new argument about sealing it with oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה clearly forbids wax. The question now is oil, which is thick and can block a hole but is not smoothed into place like wax. רב forbids it and שמואל allows it.

phrases.english: The mishna said: And if it was perforated, etc.
Oil — Rav forbade, and Shmuel permits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב forbids sealing a barrel hole with oil; שמואל permits it.

steps.title: The reasoning behind each side
steps.stepSummary: רב forbids oil as a גזירה because of wax; שמואל does not make that גזירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who forbids holds we make a גזירה because of wax. The one who permits holds we do not make a גזירה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why each one holds his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Oil by itself is not the problem. רב worries that if oil is allowed, people will also use wax, which the משנה forbids. שמואל does not worry about this.

phrases.english: The one who forbids — we decree because of wax.
And the one who permits — we do not decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasons for the two views in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The argument is whether to make a גזירה on oil because of wax.

steps.title: Did רב really forbid oil?
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר בר חנה tells רב יוסף that he himself once quoted רב as clearly permitting oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר בר חנה said to רב יוסף: You told us clearly in the name of רב that oil is permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: Someone challenges the claim that רב forbids oil. He remembers רב יוסף quoting רב as allowing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This attacks the report in step 16, not the logic in step 17. If רב permits oil, then רב and שמואל do not argue at all. The גמרא gives no reply, so the challenge stands: by this testimony, רב himself permits sealing with oil.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר בַּר חָנָה לְרַב יוֹסֵף:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar bar Ḥana said to Rav Yosef:
You told us explicitly in Rav's name —
Oil is permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the report of רב's opinion from step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב forbids sealing with oil
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יוסף himself had quoted רב as clearly permitting oil, which contradicts the report.

steps.title: שמואל forbids using a myrtle leaf as a spout
steps.stepSummary: טבות the hunter quotes שמואל that using a myrtle leaf as a spout in a barrel is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: טבות the hunter said in the name of שמואל: this myrtle leaf is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling: you may not put a myrtle leaf into a barrel's hole to make the wine flow out on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is surprising, since we just ruled that a cut reed may be used as a spout. The rule does not give its reason yet, so the גמרא will ask next.

phrases.english: Tavut the hunter said that Shmuel said:
This myrtle leaf — it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ruling about a different kind of spout.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Using a myrtle leaf as a spout in a barrel is forbidden.

steps.title: Why is the myrtle leaf forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind שמואל's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the leaf is forbidden. This sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting a leaf in a hole is not itself a מלאכה. So the גמרא wants to know what worry stands behind the rule.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the rule in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the myrtle leaf is forbidden

steps.title: רב יימר: a decree because of a real spout
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר from דפתי says it is a גזירה, so people do not come to make a real spout.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יימר from דפתי said: it is a גזירה because of a spout.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer: the leaf looks like a spout, so the רבנן forbade it in case someone makes a real one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is about the final shape, not about where the leaf came from. Rolling a leaf into a spout is too close to making a real spout on שבת.

phrases.english: Rav Yeimar of Difti said:
It is a decree because of a spout.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה so that one will not make an actual spout.

steps.title: רב אשי: a decree in case he cuts a leaf
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the worry is that someone will cut a leaf off the branch on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: it is a גזירה in case he cuts one off.
steps.whatsHappening: A second, different answer to the same question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the worry is not the spout's shape but the cutting of a leaf from the branch. This is like the reed case, where the fear was cutting a new reed.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
It is a decree lest he cut one off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another answer to step 20, different from step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה so that one will not cut a leaf off the branch.

steps.title: What difference do the two reasons make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical case would be judged differently by the two reasons.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks when the two reasons would give different rulings. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree the leaf is forbidden. The גמרא wants a real case where only one of the reasons would apply.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two answers in steps 21 and 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two reasons give different rulings

steps.title: The difference: leaves already cut and set aside
steps.stepSummary: The two reasons differ about leaves that were already cut and put aside before שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is leaves that were already cut and set aside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: if the leaves were cut before שבת, the two reasons lead to different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב אשי there is nothing left to cut, so his worry does not apply and it would be permitted. For רב יימר the leaf still looks like a spout, so it stays forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: A myrtle leaf as a spout is forbidden. רב יימר worries about making a spout, and רב אשי worries about cutting a leaf. They differ when the leaf was already cut before שבת.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them where it was already cut and set aside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Leaves cut and set aside before שבת: permitted according to רב אשי, forbidden according to רב יימר.

steps.title: רב and שמואל argue about felt cloths
steps.stepSummary: A new dispute is introduced. רב forbids felt cloths (בי סדיא) and שמואל permits them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Felt cloths: רב forbids and שמואל permits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a short dispute between רב and שמואל about felt cloths. The next lines will explain exactly what they are arguing about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Felt cloths are mostly used as something to sit on, but a person can also wrap himself in them. The question is whether he may wear one through a public area on שבת, or whether that counts as carrying a burden.

keyTerms.meaning: Felt cloths, usually sat on but sometimes worn

phrases.english: Felt cloths:
phrases.notes: Thick cloths, usually spread out to sit on.

phrases.english: Rav forbids, and Shmuel permits.
phrases.notes: The question is wearing them through a public area on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, unrelated dispute after the previous discussion about שמואל's rule ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב forbids going out wrapped in felt cloths on שבת, and שמואל permits it.

steps.title: The dispute is only about medium felt
steps.stepSummary: Everyone permits soft felt and everyone forbids hard felt. The argument is only about felt in the middle.
steps.simpleTranslation: With soft ones, everyone agrees it is permitted. With hard ones, everyone agrees it is forbidden. Where they argue is with the medium ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the dispute. It shows exactly which kind of felt רב and שמואל argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Soft felt is like a normal garment, so everyone permits it. Hard felt is clearly not clothing, so everyone forbids it. Only medium felt is unclear, and that is where the two opinions differ.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees (literally: all the world does not argue)

phrases.english: With soft ones,
everyone agrees that it is permitted.
With hard ones,
everyone agrees that it is forbidden.
Where they argue is with the medium ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the scope of the dispute just stated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Soft felt is permitted by all, hard felt is forbidden by all, and the dispute is only about medium felt.

steps.title: Does it look like carrying a burden?
steps.stepSummary: רב forbids because medium felt looks like a burden being carried. שמואל permits because it does not look that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who forbids holds that it looks like a burden, and the one who permits holds that it does not look like a burden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason behind each side of the dispute about medium felt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is about how things look, not about the cloth itself. If people see someone wrapped in medium felt, do they think he is wearing clothing or carrying a load? רב says it looks like carrying, and שמואל says it looks like wearing.

keyTerms.meaning: It looks like, it appears as
A burden, a load being carried

phrases.english: The one who forbids holds that it looks like a burden,
phrases.notes: This is רב.

phrases.english: and the one who permits holds that it does not look like a burden.
phrases.notes: This is שמואל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind each side of the medium-felt dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute depends on whether wearing medium felt looks like carrying a burden.

steps.title: רב never said this outright
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reveals that רב's forbidding opinion was never stated by him. People guessed it from something he did.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this opinion of רב was not said explicitly. Rather, it was said by inference.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions where רב's opinion really came from. It sets up a story that will explain how people reached this conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A teaching can be stated directly, or it can be guessed from how a rabbi behaved. Here the גמרא says רב's view was only guessed, which opens the door to showing that the guess was mistaken.

phrases.english: And this opinion of Rav
was not said explicitly;
rather, it was said by inference.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא דְּרַב לָאו בְּפֵירוּשׁ אִיתְּמַר אֶלָּא מִכְּלָלָא אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Re-examines the source of רב's opinion stated in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב's opinion that felt is forbidden was only inferred from his behavior.

steps.title: The story: רב would not sit on the felt
steps.stepSummary: רב came to a crowded place and sat outside in a כרמלית. People brought him felt cloths, and he did not sit on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב came to a certain place where there was no room. He went out and sat in a כרמלית. They brought him felt cloths, and he did not sit on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells the story that led people to think רב forbids felt cloths.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The felt was brought to רב through a כרמלית on שבת, probably by people wearing it. When רב refused to sit on it, onlookers assumed he refused because the felt had been brought in a forbidden way.

keyTerms.meaning: An in-between area on שבת, neither fully private nor fully public

phrases.english: For Rav happened to come to a certain place
where there was no room for him,
phrases.notes: There was not enough room inside for him and his students.

phrases.english: so he went out and sat in a karmelit.
They brought him felt cloths,
and he did not sit on them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the event from which רב's opinion was inferred.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב refused to sit on felt cloths that had been brought to him in a כרמלית.

steps.title: The wrong conclusion and the real reason
steps.stepSummary: Onlookers thought רב forbids felt, but that is not true. רב publicly declared it permitted, and he refused to sit only out of respect for his colleagues.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever saw it thought it was because felt cloths are forbidden. But that is not so, for רב used to announce publicly that felt cloths are permitted. He did not sit on them out of respect for our Rabbis.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the conclusion people drew from the story and gives רב's real reason for not sitting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The behavior was real, but the explanation was wrong. רב did not want to sit higher and more comfortably than the important rabbis sitting with him. So according to this, רב actually permits felt cloths.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not leave this sugya thinking רב forbids felt. The גמרא shows that the forbidding view was a mistaken guess, and that רב himself publicly permitted it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches a general lesson: a ruling inferred from a rabbi's behavior can be wrong, because he may have acted for a completely different reason.

phrases.english: Whoever saw it thought
that it was because felt cloths are forbidden.
But that is not so,
for Rav used to announce publicly:
felt cloths are permitted.
And it was out of respect for our Rabbis
that he did not sit on it.
phrases.notes: He did not want to sit on a more honored seat than them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn from the story in step 29.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that רב forbids felt cloths.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Onlookers misread why רב acted. He held back out of respect, not because of any prohibition.

steps.title: Who were those rabbis?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the rabbis were that רב was honoring.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who were they?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short follow-up question about the identity of the rabbis in the story. The next line gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a simple clarifying question. It does not challenge anything. It only fills in a detail of the story.

phrases.english: And who were they?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a detail mentioned in step 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the rabbis רב was honoring.

steps.title: They were רב כהנא and רב אסי
steps.stepSummary: The rabbis were רב כהנא and רב אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא and רב אסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the rabbis, which finishes the felt-cloth discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא and רב אסי were students and colleagues of רב. Even so, רב showed them honor by not sitting higher than them.

keyTerms.meaning: רב כהנא, a student and colleague of רב
רב אסי, a student and colleague of רב

steps.whatToRemember: Felt cloths: soft ones are permitted by all, hard ones are forbidden by all, and medium ones were disputed. רב's forbidding view was only guessed from his behavior, and in truth he publicly permitted them.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana and Rav Asi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rabbis were רב כהנא and רב אסי.

steps.title: משנה: keeping food and water cool or warm
steps.stepSummary: The משנה permits putting food in a pit to protect it, putting good water into bad water to cool it, and putting cold water in the sun to warm it.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may put a cooked dish into a pit so that it will be protected, good water into bad water so that it will cool, and cold water in the sun so that it will warm up.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists simple things a person may do on שבת to keep food cool or to warm water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case changes the temperature of food or water without any direct cooking or forbidden work. Putting water in the sun is allowed because the sun's heat does not count as cooking.

keyTerms.meaning: So that they will cool off

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One may put a cooked dish into a pit
so that it will be protected,
phrases.notes: Protected from heat, so it does not spoil.

phrases.english: and good water into bad water,
phrases.notes: A vessel of drinkable water is put into colder, undrinkable water.

phrases.english: so that it will cool off.
And cold water in the sun
so that it will warm up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה, unrelated to the felt-cloth discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is permitted to put food in a pit to protect it, to cool water in other water, and to warm water in the sun on שבת.

steps.title: משנה: clothes that fell into water
steps.stepSummary: If clothes fell into water on the road, a person may keep walking in them. At the outer courtyard he may spread them in the sun, but not where people can see.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone whose clothes fell into water on the road may walk in them and need not worry. When he reaches the outer courtyard, he spreads them in the sun, but not in front of people.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a second case: what to do with clothes that got wet on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wearing wet clothes is not considered wringing or washing them, so he need not worry. He may dry them in the sun, but not in public view, because people might think he washed them on שבת.

phrases.english: Someone whose clothes fell into water on the road
may walk in them and need not worry.
phrases.notes: He need not worry about wringing or washing.

phrases.english: When he reaches the outer courtyard,
he spreads them in the sun,
but not in front of the public.
phrases.notes: People might suspect he washed them on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with a second case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person may walk in wet clothes and dry them in the sun, but not in public view.

steps.title: Isn't the first rule obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needed to teach that food may be put in a pit, since that seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה by asking why the first rule needed to be taught at all. The next line will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting a pot into a pit involves no forbidden work, so the rule seems too simple to need teaching. The challenge is about why the משנה bothered to say it, not about whether the rule is true.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גמרא, the discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: Gemara:
It is obvious!
phrases.notes: Refers to putting a dish into a pit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the first rule of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that one may put a dish into a pit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule seems obviously permitted, so there is no reason for the משנה to state it.

steps.title: We might have feared leveling holes
steps.stepSummary: The rule was needed because we might have made a decree forbidding it, out of fear that the person would level holes in the pit.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: let us make a decree because of leveling holes. So the משנה teaches us that there is no such decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why the rule needed to be taught. There was a possible reason to forbid it, and the משנה tells us we do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When setting a pot into the dirt of a pit, a person might smooth out bumps and holes, which is a forbidden kind of work. We might have made a protective decree because of this, but the משנה teaches that no decree was made.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us make a protective decree
Leveling holes, smoothing out the ground

steps.whatToRemember: The rule about putting food in a pit seems obvious, but the משנה teaches it to show that the חכמים did not make a decree out of fear of leveling holes.

phrases.english: You might have said:
let us make a decree because of leveling holes,
phrases.notes: He might smooth the dirt while placing the pot.

phrases.english: so it teaches us that there is no such decree.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְתֵימָא נִיגְזַר מִשּׁוּם אַשְׁווֹיֵי גוּמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 35.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא, showing that the rule is not obvious after all
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have forbidden it as a decree, out of fear of leveling holes in the pit.
steps.terutzMaskana: No decree was made, and it is permitted to put food in a pit.

steps.title: Why teach that good water may be put into bad water?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next clause of the משנה and asks why it needed to be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said you may put good water into bad water to cool it. But that is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about cooling good drinking water by placing it in bad water. It complains that this rule is too obvious to need teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cooling something is not cooking, so nothing here even looks like a שבת problem. If nothing is wrong, why would the משנה bother to say it is allowed?

keyTerms.meaning: good water, meaning drinkable fresh water
bad water, meaning cold water that is not fit to drink

phrases.english: "And good water into bad water."
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה. Bad water is cold, so the good water cools down inside it.

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same 'why is this needed?' pattern as step 35, now applied to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's clause permitting good water to be placed in bad water.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cooling involves no forbidden act and nothing that looks like one, so stating that it is permitted seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The clause is there because of the next clause
steps.stepSummary: The real חידוש is in the following clause, and the obvious clause is included alongside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The later clause is the one the משנה really needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees that the good-water case is obvious. It explains that the משנה wrote it only because of the next case, which does need to be taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה sometimes lists an easy case together with a harder one. Here the important lesson is in the סיפא, cold water placed in the sun.

keyTerms.meaning: the later clause of a משנה
it was needed for him (the תנא)

phrases.english: The latter clause was needed for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 37 by moving the חידוש to the next clause.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concedes the clause is obvious and explains it is included because of the clause that follows it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every clause of the משנה must teach its own new idea.
steps.terutzMaskana: The good-water clause is obvious. The new idea is in the סיפא about cold water in the sun.

steps.title: Cold water in the sun also seems obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the סיפא is needed, since leaving cold water in the sun also seems plainly permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said you may put cold water in the sun. This is also obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks the clause that was supposed to carry the lesson. Warming water in the sun also seems clearly allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Heating with the sun is not cooking with fire, so it is permitted on שבת. If that is so, what new thing does this clause teach?

keyTerms.meaning: the sun, or the sun's heat

phrases.english: "And cold water in the sun"
phrases.notes: This quotes the last part (the סיפא) of the משנה.

phrases.english: This too is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 38. The clause it relied on also seems obvious.
steps.kashyaTarget: The סיפא permitting cold water to be placed in the sun.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The sun is not fire, so warming water this way is plainly permitted and needs no teaching.

steps.title: No decree out of fear of wrapping the water in hot ashes
steps.stepSummary: We might have forbidden sun-warming in case the person goes on to insulate the water in hot ashes. The משנה teaches that there is no such decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said we should make a decree, because maybe he will come to wrap it in hot ashes. So the משנה teaches us that it is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the new idea in the סיפא. The משנה tells us not to forbid sun-warming as a safeguard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wrapping food or water in hot ashes (רמץ) is forbidden on שבת. Someone used to warming water without fire might slide into doing that. We might have expected a גזירה against sun-warming, but the משנה rules there is none.

keyTerms.meaning: to insulate or bury in order to keep warm

steps.confusionAlert: Reading this as 'we do issue a decree' would be a slip. The משנה permits cold water in the sun, so the lesson is that we do NOT make this decree.

phrases.english: You might have said: let us decree against it
lest he come to insulate it in hot ashes,
so it teaches us that we do not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 39 in the same way step 36 answered step 35: we might have expected a גזירה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: הוה אמינא of a protective decree, rejected by the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Forbid warming water in the sun so the person will not come to wrap it in hot ashes.
steps.terutzMaskana: No decree is made. Cold water may be placed in the sun on שבת.

steps.title: What is forbidden for appearance is forbidden even in private
steps.stepSummary: On the case of clothes that fell into water, רב יהודה quotes רב: a מראית העין prohibition applies even in the most private room.
steps.simpleTranslation: "One whose clothes fell into water" and so on. רב יהודה said in the name of רב: wherever the חכמים forbade something because of how it looks, it is forbidden even in the innermost rooms.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה about clothes that fell into water. It quotes רב's general rule that a prohibition based on appearance does not disappear when no one is watching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מראית העין rule exists so that onlookers will not suspect a person of breaking a law. You might expect it to apply only in public. רב says the חכמים made no distinction, so it holds even in total privacy.

keyTerms.meaning: fell, here meaning the clothes fell into water
how it looks, meaning an act forbidden because people may suspect wrongdoing
the innermost rooms, fully private places

steps.whyThisMatters: רב's rule of מראית העין is a major general principle in הלכה, applied well beyond this case.

phrases.english: "One whose clothes fell" and so on.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה summarized in step 34.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Wherever the Sages prohibited something
because of how it appears,
it is forbidden even in the innermost rooms.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the water clauses and opens a new topic on the wet-clothes משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A rabbinic prohibition based on מראית העין applies even in complete privacy.

steps.title: Our משנה forbids drying only in public
steps.stepSummary: The משנה forbids spreading clothes only where people can see, which implies privacy is allowed. That contradicts רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: he may spread them in the sun, but not in front of people!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's rule using our own משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Drying clothes is forbidden here only because onlookers might think he washed them. The משנה limits the ban to public view, so in private it is allowed. רב said appearance-based bans apply even in private.

keyTerms.meaning: in front of the people, in public view

phrases.english: We learned: he may spread them in the sun
but not in front of the people!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's rule from step 41.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that מראית העין prohibitions apply even in private.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה bans drying only in public view, which implies that in private it is permitted. This contradicts רב.

steps.title: A dispute between תנאים: רב follows רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון forbid drying even in private. רב follows them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute between תנאים, as a ברייתא taught: he may spread them in the sun, but not in front of people. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון forbid it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that our משנה reflects only one opinion. Other תנאים agree with רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא allows drying in private, matching our משנה. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון forbid it even in private, which is exactly רב's rule. So רב has strong support, even if the משנה follows the other view.

keyTerms.meaning: it is a dispute between תנאים
as it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: רב: what is forbidden because of appearance is forbidden even in private. This matches רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון. Our משנה follows the תנא קמא, who allows drying in private.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of Tannaim,
as it was taught: he may spread them in the sun
but not in front of the people.
Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon forbid it.
phrases.notes: They forbid it even in private, as רב rules.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves step 42 by showing רב sides with other תנאים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute between תנאים. The opposing source reflects only one side.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is unanimous, so רב contradicts it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows the תנא קמא. רב follows רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון.

steps.title: רב הונא begins a new statement
steps.stepSummary: An attribution line opens a new statement by רב הונא, which continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said:
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. רב הונא is about to say something, and his actual words come on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the name of the speaker appears here. The content of his statement comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא, a student of רב

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement begins after the מראית העין discussion is resolved.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated. It continues on the next amud.
